States already claim dominion over bodies for collective ends. Conscription seizes years of men’s lives and risk of death. Crime control and quarantine restrict movement and association. Historical states have long regulated marriage, inheritance, and fertility when survival demanded it—Sparta’s natalist pressure on warrior stock, certain imperial Chinese and Ottoman practices, and 20th-century pronatalist dictatorships that demonstrably raised cohorts during exigency. A child’s existence externalizes massive public goods (future taxpayers, soldiers, innovators) and public bads (dependency, disorder).
